title: TokenForge
subtitle: AI-Powered Design System Token Generator
overview: TokenForge turns natural language into production-ready design tokens in seconds. Instead of manually building a design system, users describe their brand and TokenForge generates an accessible, developer-ready foundation.
problem: Most design systems begin with repetitive manual work: colors, typography, spacing, shadows, radii and naming. These decisions consume time before product design starts. Four challenges stood out: creation is repetitive, manual decisions cause inconsistency, accessibility is often overlooked, and existing tools can't interpret a brand's personality.
solution: A platform where users describe their brand and receive a complete, accessible design system in under 60 seconds. TokenForge generates semantic color palettes, type scales, spacing, radius and shadow systems with WCAG compliance built in. Users keep full editing control, and tokens export as CSS Variables, Tailwind Configuration or JSON.

features.title: AI Brand Interpretation
features.description: Users describe their product naturally — for example 'A calm, professional fintech platform for West African users' — and the AI converts it into structured design tokens.

features.title: Automated Token Generation
features.description: Creates semantic color palettes, typography scales, spacing systems, border radius values and shadow systems from a single prompt.

features.title: Live Preview
features.description: Generated tokens are immediately applied to sample interfaces including buttons, forms, cards and navigation, with no refresh required.

features.title: Manual Overrides
features.description: Every generated token stays editable, and changes update the preview instantly without refreshing the page.

features.title: Accessibility Checker
features.description: Automatically evaluates color combinations against WCAG standards and highlights combinations that fail contrast requirements.

features.title: Export Options
features.description: Export tokens as CSS Variables, Tailwind Configuration or JSON, bridging the gap between design and development.

features.title: Remix
features.description: Users can generate multiple AI variations from an existing design system instead of starting over.

architecture.title: Prompt-to-Token Pipeline
architecture.description: TokenForge uses a natural language pipeline that parses brand descriptions into design decisions. The output is a structured token set that maps to CSS custom properties, Tailwind config keys and JSON schemas. The live preview layer renders these tokens against real UI components in real time.
highlights: Natural language parsing for brand interpretation

results.description: From brand description to complete design system
Automatic WCAG compliance evaluation on all color pairs

sections.title: Research
sections.content: We explored existing design-system workflows and found that most tools focus on editing existing systems rather than generating new ones. That revealed an opportunity to simplify the earliest stage of product design.

sections.title: User Flow
sections.content: The experience was designed to require minimal learning: describe the brand, select optional mood and industry, generate the system, preview the UI, edit tokens if needed, validate accessibility and export.

sections.title: Design Decisions
sections.content: We replaced dozens of configuration inputs with a conversational prompt, lowering the learning curve for beginners while speeding up experienced designers. Seeing tokens applied immediately builds confidence, semantic naming scales across teams, and accessibility is built into generation rather than added later.

sections.title: Challenges
sections.content: The biggest challenge was balancing automation with control. Generating everything without customization feels restrictive; configuring everything manually loses the speed advantage. We solved it with a hybrid workflow: AI creates the initial system and users retain full editing control.

sections.title: What I Learned
sections.content: This project pushed me to think about design systems as products, AI-assisted experiences, accessibility-first workflows, developer handoff and cross-functional collaboration. It reinforced that great design is not just beautiful screens, but systems that help people work more efficiently.
